hints: Look at what W is made from and what it makes. Only C, H and N going to a carboxylic acid with aqueous acid should remind you of one special hydrolysis.
Recall that acid hydrolysis of a nitrile keeps all its carbons, with the $\text{-C}\equiv\text{N}$ carbon becoming the $\text{-COOH}$ carbon. Propanoic acid has three carbons in total.
Use nitrile naming where the nitrile carbon is counted as carbon 1, so a three-carbon acid must come from a three-carbon nitrile.
walkthrough:
**Narrow down the functional group**

Think like a detective. W contains only $\text{C}$, $\text{H}$ and $\text{N}$.

The two common choices here are amine ($\text{-NH}_2$) and nitrile ($\text{-C}\equiv\text{N}$). Amines react with $\text{HCl}$ to form ammonium salts, not carboxylic acids.

**Recall nitrile acid hydrolysis**

Nitriles are hydrolysed on heating with aqueous acid to give a carboxylic acid plus an ammonium ion. This is the key reaction:
$$\text{R-C}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{HCl(aq), heat}} \text{R-COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Match the carbon skeleton**

Propanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, which has 3 carbons in total.

The $\text{-COOH}$ carbon came directly from the $\text{-C}\equiv\text{N}$ carbon, so W must also have 3 carbons. A 3-carbon nitrile is propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$.

options.A: Incorrect. Ethylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, is an amine. Amines are bases and react with $\text{HCl(aq)}$ to give alkylammonium salts like $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_3^+\text{Cl}^-$, they never hydrolyse to form propanoic acid.
options.B: Incorrect functional group is right but name is wrong. Ethanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$, has only 2 carbons. Its acid hydrolysis would give ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, not propanoic acid.
options.C: Incorrect. Propylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, is an amine. Like all amines it would simply be protonated by $\text{HCl}$ to form a salt. It cannot be converted into a carboxylic acid by hydrolysis.
options.D: Correct. Propanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$, contains only C, H and N and has the nitrile functional group. Heating with $\text{HCl(aq)}$ hydrolyses it to propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, with the same 3-carbon skeleton.
